text:
acme_netops: Hey @marie_support, since last night our service calls to our Redwood Private endpoint (private.redwood.acme.internal) are failing when traffic goes through our BlueGate corporate gateway. Apps return intermittent 502/SSL errors. curl shows 'SSL: no shared cipher'. Any ideas?

marie_support: sorry you're hitting this — can you paste the exact curl/openssl output and confirm whether this is happening only when traffic goes through BlueGate? :eyes:

acme_netops: Confirmed only via BlueGate. Direct-hosted VPC connection from our dev box (no corporate gateway) succeeds. Copying paste from a failing host: 

```
$ curl -v https://private.redwood.acme.internal/v1/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://private.redwood.acme.internal/v1/health
*   Trying 10.5.32.11:443...
* Connected to private.redwood.acme.internal (10.5.32.11) port 443 (#0)
* TLS 1.0 connection using ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256
* SSL: no shared cipher
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) SSL: no shared cipher
```

acme_netops: We also tried from a different host behind BlueGate and saw the same.

marie_support: thanks. Can you run an openssl s_client test from the failing host and include output? Use -servername to send SNI. Eg: `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.internal -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE' -debug`

acme_netops: Pasting the failing s_client output we got: 

```
$ openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.internal -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE' -debug
CONNECTED(00000003)
140056789012000:error:1408F10B:SSL routines:ssl3_get_record:wrong version number:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:
---
no peer certificate available
---
No client certificate CA names sent
---
SSL handshake has read 7 bytes and written 319 bytes
---
New, (NONE), Cipher is (NONE)
```

marie_support: that 'wrong version number' often indicates the gateway is doing TLS bridging/termination or talking plain HTTP to the upstream. Two axes to check: (1) BlueGate TLS interception (man-in-the-middle) re-signing certs and restricting ciphers, (2) whether BlueGate is speaking plain HTTP to our origin (port mismatch).

ivan_neteng: adding some detail — some enterprise gateways enforce a FIPS cipher suite set or RSA-only KEX. Redwood's private endpoints prefer ECDHE ephemeral key exchange (ECDHE-RSA). If the gateway strips or rewrites cipher lists, you can get 'no shared cipher'.

ivan_neteng: please run these from the failing host and paste outputs: 
1) `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.internal -tls1_2 -cipher 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' -ign_eof`
2) `openssl s_client -connect private.redwood.acme.internal:443 -servername private.redwood.acme.internal -tls1_2 -cipher 'RSA' -ign_eof`
3) `curl -v --tlsv1.2 --ciphers 'ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256' https://private.redwood.acme.internal/v1/health`

acme_netops: Ran them. ECDHE test fails with the same 'wrong version number'. The RSA-only cipher test actually completes the TCP TCP/TLS handshake but the certificate subject is BlueGate-Intercept-CA (so BlueGate is re-signing). Example: `subject=/CN=private.redwood.acme.internal (re-signed by BlueGate-Intercept-CA)`

acme_netops: So BlueGate is doing TLS interception and re-signing certs, and it appears to only allow RSA key-exchange to the origin or is downgrading the connection.

marie_support: thanks — that proves the gateway is doing MITM and re-signing. Two immediate things: 
- We need BlueGate to forward SNI to the origin and allow ECDHE ciphers (recommended: at least TLS1.2 with ECDHE suites).
- If BlueGate is re-signing with its own CA, ensure its re-signed chain includes key-exchange algorithms compatible with our runtime, or configure their MITM to allow passthrough for our IPs.

marie_support: Can you ask BlueGate team to allow the following TLS profile to the Redwood IPs / hostnames: TLSv1.2+, ciphers: `ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256`, `ECDHE-RSA-AES256-GCM-SHA384`, and to preserve SNI. Also request they do not downgrade to SSLv3/RSA-only KEX.

alex_engineer: adding engineering note — our runtime publishes only ephemeral ECDHE suites by default for forward secrecy. We can add a temporary RSA KEX fallback for Private endpoints, but that requires an infra rollout and security sign-off (it weakens forward secrecy). Haley, any concerns?

haley_security: RSA fallback is a mitigation but reduces forward secrecy. If customer absolutely needs it and BlueGate cannot be changed, we'd prefer a scoped exception: allow RSA-only ciphers for the specific private endpoint IPs and limit to TLS1.2 with strict monitoring. Also collect packet captures to verify no credential leakage.

acme_netops: BlueGate team responded: they cannot disable interception globally, but they can allow TLS passthrough for a short list of hosts. They asked what exact IPs and SNI we need to whitelist.

marie_support: give them these IPs (redacted here for thread) and ask for TCP passthrough for port 443 or to preserve SNI and support the ECDHE cipher list. Request logs of the handshake from BlueGate if they continue to re-sign.

ivan_neteng: I'm going to escalate to eng-runtime to evaluate adding a temporary RSA KEX fallback flag for Private endpoints behind corporate gateways. Ticket created: INF-1228. Tagging @alex_engineer and @haley_security.

sre-bot: Incident note created — INF-1228. Priority: P2.

acme_netops: Quick question — if we do passthrough, do we need any cert changes on the Redwood side?

alex_engineer: No cert changes required if passthrough preserves TCP to origin and forwards SNI. If BlueGate continues to re-sign, we need their CA installed in clients or an exception.

marie_support: Next steps for customer: 1) ask BlueGate to do TCP passthrough for private.redwood.acme.internal (range provided), OR allow ECDHE cipher suites and preserve SNI. 2) If passthrough isn't possible, get BlueGate to provide their re-signed cert chain + handshake logs and a pcap of a failing handshake. 3) We'll keep INF-1228 open and circle back with an engineering mitigation if needed.

acme_netops: OK we'll request passthrough and share the BlueGate handshake logs if they resist. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:

marie_support: thanks — marking as escalated and will update once eng has an assessment. :thumbsup:
